title: Personal Portfolio - Full Technical Overview
text:
This is Ikeoluwa Oladele's personal portfolio site, built from scratch as both a showcase and a technical project in its own right. It consists of two independently deployable parts: a Vue 3 single-page application for the frontend and a Python FastAPI backend deployed on Azure App Service for Containers.

The most distinctive feature is the AI chatbot embedded in the bottom-right corner of every page. It is context-aware - when a visitor is browsing a specific project, the bot knows which project is in focus and can answer questions about it specifically. The chatbot uses a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: incoming questions are first checked against a topic gate, and only on-topic questions proceed to retrieval. Retrieval fans out across project namespaces in Pinecone and the best results are passed to Google Gemini for generation.

Project data is pulled live from GitHub. Any public repository belonging to TheBluCoder and tagged with the 'portfolio' GitHub topic can be ingested into Pinecone. Each repo's README and optional .github/project.json metadata file are fetched, chunked, and stored in a namespace named github:TheBluCoder:<repo-name>. A GitHub webhook triggers re-ingestion on supported repository events, and extra context can be manually uploaded through the admin API.

The frontend is built with Vue 3, Vite, and Tailwind CSS v4. Pages include a home section, an about page, a projects browser, a gallery, and a resume page. The projects page fetches live data from the backend and falls back to a static JSON file when needed. The chat panel maintains separate conversation histories per project, and markdown responses are rendered with markdown-it.

The backend uses FastAPI with Pydantic for validation and runs in a custom container on Azure App Service for Containers. Storage uses Azure Table Storage for the gallery, reading list, and rate-limit counters, with in-process memory fallback for local development. Rate limiting is based on a visitor fingerprint built from IP and User-Agent.

The resume page parses a PDF hosted on Google Drive using pdfplumber, then sends the extracted text to Gemini to produce a structured JSON object. The parsed result is cached for 24 hours, and the admin can flush it through the API.

The gallery section displays poems written by Ikeoluwa, supports likes, and supports moderated comments. The admin dashboard endpoints allow poem management, comment moderation, reading list updates, and resume cache invalidation.
